conviction_note: The only bar is one analyst (Inderes: Q3 EBIT 8.0 MEUR, EPS 0.15). It depends on about 1.7 MEUR of non-accrued PE performance fees, against 0.73 MEUR in Q2, and Inderes's FY26e implies a Q4 of about 12 MEUR EBIT. So the print more likely lands below the bar (print_vs_bar about -8%). But misses against this one analyst have not been sold: the Q2'26 EBIT miss of -12% closed +2.1%, and Q3'25 closed -0.45%. The stock is already down about 15% (ex-dividend) since the Q2 print, and the qualitative outlook is likely to be repeated. That keeps p_up at 45 on an abs_move of 4.0, so the scaled number is -0.4. The findings sum to -1.3 because each is sized on its own, and the gap between the two is the reaction veto plus the sell-side discount the price already carries.

already_public.what: Event date and time: Q3 2026 interim report Friday 23 Oct 2026 at about 08:00 Helsinki, press conference 11:00

H1 2026: revenue 29.6 MEUR, EBIT 11.6, EPS 0.22. Q2 EBIT 6.0, Q2 PE performance fees 1.59 MEUR (0.73 paid non-accrued + 0.87 catch-up), PE performance-fee cash flow 6.0 MEUR in H1. Qualitative outlook: real estate management fees down in 2026, PE fees up, one more fund structure expected to enter the performance-fee cash-flow phase during the rest of the year
The company's own estimate puts the 2026 catch-up accrual at 3.4 MEUR, of which 1.746 was booked in H1, leaving about 0.83 per quarter for H2 (Inderes models 0.9 for Q3)

Second dividend instalment of EUR 0.26, record date 7 Oct, so ex-dividend 6 Oct 2026

new_in_release.expect: Q3 PE performance fees. The Q3 catch-up accrual of about 0.85 MEUR is near-certain; paid non-accrued fees of about 1.7 MEUR are needed to reach the bar and are more likely to come in short (Q2 was 0.73). EBIT is more likely around 7.0-7.5 than 8.0, but the fees are lumpy and could beat.

The qualitative outlook is likely to be repeated (Inderes expects that). Whether the third PE fund structure entered the cash-flow phase in Q3 is the swing item for the Q4 view. Unknown, with a slight lean toward 'not yet large enough' to support FY26e EBIT of 31.9.

Q3 PE fundraising (Inderes about 70 MEUR, plus the PE Multi-Strategy launch), the redemption queue in the real estate funds, and AUM after traditional outflows of about -210 MEUR. Mixed, slight negative.
PE performance-fee cash flow should be well above the P&L figure (Inderes says so). That is a possible positive talking point, as in Q2.
None expected in Q3 (the second 2025 instalment was paid on 14 Oct).

findings.finding: The single-analyst Q3 EBIT bar of 8.0 MEUR needs about 1.7 MEUR of paid, non-accrued PE performance fees on top of the 0.9 MEUR catch-up the company has effectively pre-announced. Q2 delivered 0.73 MEUR of non-accrued fees, and the same analyst has overestimated recent prints (Q2'26 EBIT 6.0 vs 6.9e, -12%; Q3'25 EPS 0.15 vs 0.17 in the baseline consensus). A miss of roughly 5-12% on EBIT is the more likely outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 EBIT missed Inderes by 12% and the stock closed +2.12% on 2026-08-04 because the PE cash flow was positive. Q3'25 EPS 0.15 vs 0.17e closed -0.45% on 2025-10-21. Q1'26 'no major surprises' closed -2.0%. Misses against this bar have mostly not been sold.
findings.original_quote: Yhtiö kirjaa aiemmin kerrotun mukaisesti voitontasausta 0,9 MEUR, ja tämän lisäksi odotamme 1,7 MEUR:n tuottopalkkioita. ... Haluamme kuitenkin nähdä lisää konkretiaa kovien tuottopalkkioennusteidemme katteeksi. (The company books 0.9 MEUR of profit equalisation as previously disclosed, and on top of that we expect 1.7 MEUR of performance fees. ... We would like to see more concrete evidence to back our tough performance-fee estimates.)
findings.why_not_priced: The estimate is public, and the analyst flags the risk himself. The stock's ~15% ex-dividend fall since the Q2 print suggests the market already discounts the house numbers, which is why this is sized small. If the market fully believed 8.0 EBIT, the stock would not be on an Inderes-estimated P/E of 13 with a 7.5% yield. What is not priced is how far short of the bar the non-accrued fee line lands, and that is genuinely unknown until the print.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26: traditional net subscriptions 'reippaasti miinuksella' (sharply negative) did not stop a +2.1% day. AUM outflows have not been a measurable mover on print days.
findings.original_quote: Perinteisen varainhoidon puolella yhtiö on menettänyt Q3:n aikana merkittävästi pääomia, kun nettomerkinnät ovat olleet noin 210 MEUR pakkasella. (On the traditional asset management side the company lost significant capital during Q3, with net subscriptions about 210 MEUR negative.)
findings.why_not_priced: It is public in the preview, so it is mostly priced. The company has not yet confirmed it, and the reported AUM bridge could make it more visible. Large mandates carry low fees, so the P&L effect is small. Sized near zero for that reason.

findings.finding: Inderes's FY26e EBIT of 31.9 MEUR, with H1 actual at 11.6, implies H2 EBIT of about 20.3 MEUR, so roughly 12.3 MEUR in Q4. eQ's last six quarters ran 5.6-8.0 MEUR. The Q3 report's commentary on whether the third PE fund structure has entered the performance-fee cash-flow phase decides whether that Q4 is credible. A neutral or vague update invites FY estimate cuts on the day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The qualitative outlook has been repeated at every 2026 print (Q1 -2.0%, Q2 +2.1%). The only line that has moved the stock positively was PE performance-fee cash flow (Q2).
findings.original_quote: Tunnusluvut ... 26e ... EBIT (oik.) 31,9 ... EPS (oik.) 0,60 ... On kuitenkin selvää, että tuottopalkkioiden pitäisi kasvaa Q2:n tasolta, kun alla olevien rahastojen irtaantumiset etenevät ja myös kolmas rahasto on todennäköisesti siirtynyt voitonjakoon Q3:lla. (Key figures 2026e: adjusted EBIT 31.9, adjusted EPS 0.60 ... It is clear, however, that performance fees should rise from the Q2 level as exits in the underlying funds progress, and a third fund has probably also moved to profit distribution in Q3.)
findings.why_not_priced: The implied Q4 is arithmetic anyone can do, and the price discount suggests some have. But the confirmation or denial of the third fund's transition, and the size of its cash flow, only arrives in the release. If the market were pricing a confident 12 MEUR Q4, the stock would not have fallen ~15% (ex-dividend) since 4 August with no company news.

findings.finding: The company has already guided that real estate fund management fees fall in 2026. Both property funds still have redemption queues (eQ Yhteiskuntakiinteistöt NAV 1,048 MEUR, eQ Liikekiinteistöt 494 MEUR at 30.6.2026), and Inderes calls the latest rise in rates 'poison' for the sector. Q3 real estate fees land inside the guided decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Repeated at Q1 and Q2 2026 with no visible print-day reaction attributable to it.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced because it is inside the company's own guidance, hence near zero. What is left is whether the Q3 fund valuations (the rates move) cut the fee base faster than guided. That is macro-to-company transmission and has not been confirmed by the company.

The stock's own record of shrugging off misses against the single analyst cuts against the findings, so p_up stays at 45 rather than lower.
language_note: Inderes publishes the eQ preview in Finnish first (04:31 GMT 2026-10-16), with AI-translated Swedish/Danish copies. No English version of the Q3 preview was found. lessons_applied: 'Size the move on what is new; let reaction history move p_up, not abs_move' raised abs_move_pct from 3.5 to 4.0. The draft had been partly anchored to this name's ~1.8% median print-day reaction. The Q3 numbers are not pre-released, coverage is one analyst and turnover is $147k a day, against a reiterated-guide base of about 2.3%.
